title: The Economics of Polycrisis Resilience
subtitle: Integrating Risk Reduction, Preventive Development and Adaptive Capacity Into Economic Growth
dek: Why treating risk reduction and resilience separately from economic growth amplifies cascading disruptions—and how weaving prevention, modular utilities, adaptive capabilities, and fiscal buffers into growth strategy multiplies long-run output through 2050.
abstract: The Economics of Polycrisis Resilience examines how economic development can be structured to reduce vulnerability to interconnected systemic risks while strengthening long-term productive capacity, human development, and economic stability. Rather than treating risk reduction and emergency recovery as separate overlays managed after disruptions strike, integrating preventive investment and adaptive capacity directly into growth foundations turns resilience into a compounding driver of prosperity.

Calibrating non-linear cascade-contagion dynamics across coupled power grids, supply logistics, sovereign debt markets, and household balance sheets demonstrates why unbuffered economies forfeit 38.0% of frontier productive potential (-10.5 pts supply contagion, -9.0 pts climate/grid outages, -7.0 pts food-fuel spikes, -6.5 pts human scarring, and -5.0 pts sovereign spread penalties), stalling cumulative 2050 output at 114.5 versus 278.0 under an integrated Resilient Growth Compact.

Empirical valuations confirm a 12.2x 25-year social benefit-cost ratio (6.4x avoided disaster losses plus 5.8x continuous TFP growth) versus 1.3x–1.9x for reactive crisis stimulus: an +8.0% modular CapEx buffer cuts industrial supply recovery 90.7% (54.0 to 5.0 days) and lifts infrastructure continuity to 93/100; biometric DPI buffers retain 89%–95% 90-day household stability; sovereign spreads compress from 640 to 125 bps while private investment doubles toward 32.4% of GDP; Pooled Growth-Resilience Trusts cut financing costs to 4.0% WACC (7.8x leverage); and Global Polycrisis Resilience Parity rises from 46.5 in 2026 to 92.0 by 2050.
findings: Separating growth maximization from systemic risk reduction leaves interconnected economies vulnerable to multi-node shock cascades that erase 38.0% of potential GDP output (-10.5 pts supply contagion, -9.0 pts grid/climate outages, -7.0 pts food-fuel inflation, -6.5 pts human capital scarring, and -5.0 pts crisis debt spreads), capping 2050 unbuffered output at 114.5 vs 278.0 resilient.

Embedding preventive resilience inside baseline growth policy generates a 12.2x 25-year benefit-cost ratio—comprising 6.4x avoided cascade losses and 5.8x uninterrupted capital/TFP growth during ordinary periods—outperforming reactive crisis stimulus (1.9x) and uninsured rebuild debt (1.3x) by more than sixfold.

Co-locating islandable clean microgrids, subsurface conduits, and digital supply twins for a +8.0% modular CapEx adder raises post-shock infrastructure continuity from 44 to 93 out of 100 and compresses supply-chain recovery duration 90.7% from 54.0 days down to 5.0 days.

Anticipatory biometric Digital Public Infrastructure safety nets preserve 90.0% household wage stability, 93.0% schooling continuity, 95.0% primary clinical access, and 89.0% distress-free asset survival 90 days into compound shocks, while pre-arranged 15.5% GDP 30-day fiscal buffers compress sovereign spreads from 640 to 125 bps and raise private CapEx from 15.2% to 32.4% of GDP.

Merging divided economic-planning and risk ministries (flagged across 88.0% of 70 audited ministries) and syndicating 4.0% WACC Pooled Growth-Resilience Trusts (7.8x leverage) lifts per-capita output +62.0% over fragile baselines and pushes Global Polycrisis Resilience Index parity from 46.5 in 2026 to 92.0 by 2050.
method: An interconnected nonlinear cascade-propagation and endogenous sovereign-spread equilibrium model integrating 2020–2050 GDP trajectories (114.5 vs 278.0), a 38.0% cascade drag waterfall, 25-year Triple-Dividend BCR valuations (1.3x–12.2x), 12-market exposure-adaptive scatter diagnostics, infrastructure continuity stacks (44 to 93), +8.0% modularity recovery duration curves (54.0d to 5.0d), 90-day DPI safety-net panels (89%–95%), sovereign spread regressions (640 to 125 bps), a 70-ministry governance silo audit, and 10,000-draw Monte-Carlo GPRI paths (46.5 to 92.0). Comprises an executive synthesis, eight analytical sections, 16 data figures, and a calibration appendix.
